title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this page and its neighbours. A 'dispositif' (E, |o|_E) is a set E with a symmetric relation |o|, read as 'disjoint' or 'orthogonal'. For A ⊂ E write A^⊥ = {y : y |o| x for all x ∈ A}.

- Σ_E is the system of closed parts A = A^⊥⊥. It is a complete lattice with orthocomplement A ↦ A^⊥, written ∁A in the notes.
- σ_E : E → Σ_E is the map x ↦ {x}^⊥⊥.
- E carries a canonical preorder: x ≤ y iff σ(x) ⊂ σ(y).

On the previous pages Grothendieck proves a universal property. For a complete 'système' Σ (a complete lattice with orthocomplement and disjointness) and a compatible map σ : E → Σ, there is a map α : Σ_E → Σ. He builds β : Σ → Σ_E with βα = id and αβ = id, using the lemma: A ≤ B, A' ≤ B', B |o| B', A' = ∁A imply A = B and A' = B'.

This page finishes with uniqueness of α. Every A ∈ Σ_E is the sup of the σ_E(x) it majorizes, which are exactly those with x ∈ A (the underlying point set of A). So necessarily α(A) = sup_{x∈A} α(σ_E(x)) = sup_{x∈A} σ(x). In modern terms σ_E(E) is join-dense in Σ_E, so a sup-preserving extension is unique.

Then a Corollary for E' ⊂ E with the induced relation. The following are equivalent:
- (i) σ_E(E') is (join-)dense in Σ_E: every S is the sup of the elements of σ_E(E') below it.
- (ii) Restriction S ↦ S ∩ E', Σ_E → P(E'), lands in Σ_{E'} and gives an isomorphism φ : Σ_E ≅ Σ_{E'}.
- (iii) ψ : Σ_{E'} → Σ_E, S' ↦ sup σ_E(S'), is a bijection, hence an isomorphism.
- (iv) E' is dense in E for the canonical preorder.
- (v), on the next page: for x, y ∈ E, if all x' ≤ x and y' ≤ y in E' are orthogonal, then x |o| y.

Under these conditions φ and ψ are mutually inverse isomorphisms.

In modern language this is the Birkhoff polarity/Galois-closure completion of an orthogonality space (Dacey; Foulis–Randall). It is the orthogonality-space analogue of the fact that the Dedekind–MacNeille completion of a dense subset equals that of the whole: a 'density' or 'restriction' theorem. It serves to show that Σ_E is the universal complete ortho-system generated by E and depends only on a dense part of E.
errors: In (ii) Grothendieck crosses out the claim that S ↦ S∩E' maps Σ_E into Σ_{E'}. That S∩E' is E'-closed is not automatic without the density hypothesis, so (ii) must be read as 'induces a bijection Σ_E → Σ_{E'}' including the landing claim. The formulation on the page is left somewhat unsettled.
Minor slip: 'sup des éléments des éléments' is a repetition.
The implications are not proved on this page; the proofs are deferred to the next page. The next page itself warns that 'dense' is meant in the order-theoretic sense, not the topological one.

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the extension α : Σ_E → Σ because σ_E(E) is join-dense in the closure lattice
ideas.modern_name: universal property of the MacNeille-type completion (join-density gives uniqueness of a sup-preserving extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacNeille (1937), Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); for orthogonality spaces Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall

ideas.what: Equivalent conditions for a subset E' of an orthogonality space to have the same completion: join-density, restriction isomorphism, sup-map isomorphism, preorder density, orthogonality detected on E'
ideas.modern_name: density / restriction theorem for the ortholattice of closed subsets of an orthogonality space (cf. MacNeille completion of a join- and meet-dense subposet)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in lattice theory and quantum logic (Banaschewski, Schmidt for MacNeille; Foulis–Randall, Moore for orthogonality spaces)

missed.claim: Historical: in July 1986 Grothendieck was developing, in his own vocabulary ('dispositif', relation |o|, 'système' Σ_E), the theory of orthogonality spaces and their ortholattice completions, essentially the quantum-logic framework. This activity is not documented in the literature on Grothendieck. The mathematics itself is standard.
missed.quote: Soient (E, |o|_E) un dispositif ..., E' une partie de E, |o|_{E'} la relation induite. Conditions équivalentes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of biographical and historical interest for understanding Grothendieck's late, possibly 'atelier'/structural interests in 1986. It brings no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard density/restriction corollary for the closure-lattice completion of a symmetric 'disjointness' relation, known from lattice theory and quantum logic. Only the fact that Grothendieck worked on this in 1986 is mildly notable.
transcription_corrections: The page number '80' at the top is the author's numbering; the archive folio is 83.
In the crossed-out first Corollary the word after 'dispositif' looks like an adjective, possibly 'disjonctif'. Uncertain; the transcription's '[?]' is appropriate.
'Il [-reste-] {+suffit+}' should probably read 'Il reste : vu l'unicité de α, qui est immédiate, vu que ...'. The tail reads 'd'où forcément' rather than 'et α doit en ...'; the latter is struck out.
The left-margin note near (iv) reads approximately 'renvoyé aux (v)' or 'permet ... (v)' over a crossed-out word. It signals adding condition (v), stated on the next page.
(iv) reads: 'E' est dense dans E pour la relation de préordre canonique de E (induite de celle de Σ_E via σ_E)'. The prefix 'pré' is added above 'ordre'.
